• On average, total annual precipitation has increased over land areas in the United States. Since 1901, precipitation averaged across the contiguous 48 states has increased at a rate of 0.18 inches per decade.
  • When averaged over the contiguous states, total annual precipitation is projected to continue to increase under all four greenhouse gas emissions scenarios. The graph shows some fluctuation between scenarios, but by the end of this century, higher emissions will correspond to higher precipitation.
  • Climate models for all scenarios suggest that some parts of the South and Southwest will experience less precipitation in the future, while much of the rest of the country will receive more. This does not necessarily mean more water availability, however, because evaporation will also increase in a warmer climate. Climate models generally suggest that in the future, rain will occur in more intense events with longer dry spells between those events.
